title: Convert Doubly Linked List to Array I
statement:
You get `head`, the first node of a doubly linked list. Every node has an integer `val`, a `next` link to the node after it (`null` at the last node) and a `prev` link to the node before it (`null` at the first node). Return an array holding the values of all the nodes in list order, from the head to the last node.

Each case is written as `[head]`: the list's values from the first node to the last. The judge builds the linked nodes from it and passes your function the first one. (The TypeScript starter types the nodes as `ListNode`, which does not list `prev`; the objects still have it.)
constraints: The list has between 1 and 50 nodes
notes:
## Intuition

Although every node also points backwards, reading the list needs only the forward links. The head is already the first node, so start there, write down its value, follow `next`, and repeat until `next` runs out. The `prev` links would matter only if you were handed a node in the middle or at the end; walking from the tail back along `prev` and reversing gives the same array, which is a handy way to check both directions of the links.

## Approach

1. Create an empty array `values` and start `node` at `head`.
2. While `node` is not `null`, push `node.val` and move `node` to `node.next`.
3. When the walk falls off the last node, return `values`.

## Example 1, step by step

`head = [1,2,3,4,3,2,1]`. The walk starts at the head and pushes 1, then follows `next` and pushes 2, 3, 4, 3, 2 and 1 in turn. The last node's `next` is `null`, so the loop ends and `values = [1,2,3,4,3,2,1]` is returned.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every node is visited once.
- Space: O(1) apart from the returned array of n values.

## Pitfalls

- Test `node !== null` before reading `node.val`; the last node's `next` is `null`.
- Move `node` forward inside the loop, or the walk never ends.
- Repeated values (Example 2) are copied as they are; nothing is removed or sorted.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `values` | values collected so far, in list order |
| `node` | the node the walk is at, `null` after the last one |

narration.2: The answer array starts empty and fills up in list order.
narration.3: Begin the walk at the head, the first node of the list.
narration.4: Keep going while there is a node to read; the last node's next is null.
narration.6: Follow the forward link to the following node.
narration.8: The walk has passed the last node; every value is collected in order.
